verses.1: And there was a man from the people of Benjamin whose name was Meqabyos.
verses.3: And he found them and said to them, "Do not bow down and do not sacrifice to the gods of Sidon the king, as he has commanded."
verses.4: "And if you refuse, I will seize you and bring you before the king, and all your possessions will be plundered, as the king has commanded."
verses.5: And they answered and said to him, "These good and upright men—there is One to whom we bow: the God of our fathers, the Creator of heaven and earth and sea and all that is in them, who created the sun and the moon and the stars and the clouds. He is the true God, whom we worship and in whom we believe."
verses.6: And these were the nobles of the king, the four commanders, each in his own district, who were plundering the property of their fields.
verses.7: And when they wished to seize these saints, they escaped from their hands, and there was none who could touch them; and they went about plundering the property of their fields, for they were faithful and upright, steadfast and exceedingly mighty.
verses.8: And there was among them one who would kill while wringing its neck, and would strangle it like a chicken at once.
verses.9: And there was among them one who would kill a lion with a single blow of a stone, or with a strike of wood, at one time.
verses.10: And there was among them one in battle who would kill a hundred at one time with a single sword; and thus their name and their memory were renowned in all the land of Moab and among the Chaldeans.
verses.11: And they were steadfast in their faith with power, and they had wisdom and favor and speech.
verses.12: And their understanding was a wonder to their companions, and above all, the understanding of their heart was strong because they loved the Lord and did not fear death.
verses.13: And when the commanders feared them, there was none who could seize them; but they, being steadfast, escaped into the mountain fortress.
verses.14: But the commanders returned into the city and passed through the midst of the city, and they threatened the people of the land, saying, "If you do not bring out to us these rebels, the Meqabyan, we will burn your city with fire, and we will send word to the king and destroy your city."
verses.15: And at that time the people of the city went out—poor men and rich men, and women who were pregnant, and nursing children—and they all cried out together, and they lifted up their eyes toward the mountain and cried out to them, saying, "Do not destroy us and our city."
verses.16: And then they wept together and sought mercy from the Lord.
verses.17: And they turned their faces toward the east and prayed to the Lord, spreading out their hands together, and they said, "We have sinned against you, O Lord, these transgressors of your law and your commandment."
verses.18: "But we are not willing to obey the word of that wicked one who does not believe in your law, nor in gold and silver, in wood and in stone, the work of the hands of men."
verses.19: "And he forgets himself, like those whom he created, while you exist, his Creator, who kills and gives life; but he is a shedder of the blood of men and an eater of the flesh of men."
verses.20: "But we are not willing to see the face of that wicked one, nor to hear his word."
verses.21: "But rather, if you have commanded us, we will go to you and give our souls to death for your sake, and we will not hear the word of that wicked one when he says, 'Sacrifice to my gods.'"
verses.22: "But we, O Lord, with all our heart have trusted in you, the God of our fathers, who do your will and walk in your law, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who tests the heart and the kidneys."
verses.23: "And you examine the righteous and the sinner, and you search what is in the heart of man; and there is nothing hidden from you, nor is anything concealed before you."
verses.24: "And we have no other god besides you."
verses.25: "But rather, give us strength and steadfastness, and call us into this work which we desire for you, so that we may give our souls to death for the sake of your holy name."
verses.26: "And when you brought Israel out of the land of Egypt, you heard the prayer of Jacob; and now also we beseech you, O holy God."
verses.27: And when he appeared to them
verses.28: And their understanding increased greatly, and their faces shone more than the sun, and they were more beautiful than before.
